title: normaliseAuditScopeItem maps assessmentStatus to the correct normalizedStatus bucket
description: tasks.normalise.js normaliseAuditScopeItem: DONE={'closed','not_applicable'}, IN_PROG={'in_progress','under_review','needs_revision'}, everything else (including 'not_started', 'assigned') falls through to 'pending'.
steps: Call normaliseAuditScopeItem with a lean doc where assessmentStatus='closed'
Call it again with assessmentStatus='under_review'
Call it again with assessmentStatus='not_started'
Call it again with an unrecognised value, e.g. assessmentStatus='foo'
expectedResult: Returned normalizedStatus is 'done' for 'closed', 'in_progress' for 'under_review', and 'pending' for both 'not_started' and the unrecognised 'foo' value (safe default).

title: normaliseAuditScopeItem derives navigateTo/sourceEntityName from a populated vs. raw auditId
description: auditId may arrive already populated ({_id, name}, from the .populate('auditId','name') query) or as a raw ObjectId (from the WorkflowEntry legacy fallback path, which does not populate). Both must resolve navigateTo to '/audit-assurance/{id}/configured'; only the populated form yields sourceEntityName.
steps: Call normaliseAuditScopeItem with auditId = { _id: '64f...', name: 'ISO 27001 Q3 Audit' }
Call normaliseAuditScopeItem with auditId = a raw ObjectId (no populate)
Call normaliseAuditScopeItem with auditId = null
expectedResult: Both non-null cases produce navigateTo='/audit-assurance/{id}/configured' and sourceEntityId={id}; only the populated case sets sourceEntityName='ISO 27001 Q3 Audit', the raw-ObjectId case leaves sourceEntityName undefined. The null case falls back to navigateTo='/audit-assurance' with sourceEntityId undefined.

title: normaliseNonConformance surfaces requirementId from isoClauseRef
description: Regression guard for TK-011 (fixed): normaliseNonConformance previously returned no requirementId field at all, making 'audit' module tasks inconsistent (AuditScopeItem tasks show a requirement chip via TitleCell, CAR tasks did not). The fix sets requirementId: nc.isoClauseRef || null.
steps: Call normaliseNonConformance with isoClauseRef='A.5.3'
Call normaliseNonConformance with isoClauseRef omitted
expectedResult: First call returns requirementId='A.5.3'. Second call returns requirementId=null (not undefined) — TitleCell's `task.requirementId &&` check safely omits the chip either way, but the field must always be present on the object.

title: normaliseWorkflowEntry hardcodes priority='medium' and branches navigateTo/entityType by sourceModule
description: WorkflowEntry documents (evidence and policy reviews) carry no priority field, so normaliseWorkflowEntry always returns priority: 'medium' regardless of the underlying entity's real priority. navigateTo and the human-readable entityType label ('Evidence'/'Policy') are derived purely from the sourceModule argument, not from any field on the entry itself.
steps: Call normaliseWorkflowEntry(entry, 'evidence', 'evidence') on an entry with status='under_review'
Call normaliseWorkflowEntry(entry, 'policy', 'policy') on the same shaped entry
expectedResult: Both calls return priority='medium' unconditionally. The evidence call returns entityType='Evidence' and navigateTo='/evidence-management/my-reviews/{entityId}'; the policy call returns entityType='Policy' and navigateTo='/policy-management/{entityId}'. Both map status='under_review' to normalizedStatus='in_progress'.

title: normaliseEvidenceRequest always returns dueDate=undefined and isOverdue=false
description: EvidenceRequest has no dueDate field in its schema (per the inline comment in tasks.normalise.js), so normaliseEvidenceRequest hardcodes isOverdue: false directly rather than calling the shared isOverdue() helper used by every other normaliser. This is a deliberate schema-driven gap, not a bug — but it means EvidenceRequest tasks can never appear in the 'Overdue' summary card or overdue filter no matter how old the request is.
steps: Call normaliseEvidenceRequest on an EvidenceRequest doc created 90 days ago with status='open'
expectedResult: Returned task has dueDate=undefined and isOverdue=false, regardless of how old createdAt is — confirming EvidenceRequest tasks are structurally excluded from overdue detection.

title: normaliseFinding defaults remediation.status to 'open' when the remediation sub-object is absent
steps: Call normaliseFinding on a Finding doc with no 'remediation' key at all
Call normaliseFinding on a Finding doc with remediation.status='in_remediation'
Call normaliseFinding on a Finding doc with remediation.status='resolved'
expectedResult: Case 1 returns status='open', normalizedStatus='pending'. Case 2 returns normalizedStatus='in_progress'. Case 3 returns normalizedStatus='done'. No exception is thrown when 'remediation' is undefined.

title: getMyTasks null-guards assignedTo before calling .toString() in the ManagementReview and ContinuousImprovement flat-maps
description: Regression guard for TK-014 and TK-018 (both fixed): the flatMap filters in tasks.service.js read `init.assignedTo && init.assignedTo.toString() === userIdStr` (and the equivalent for ManagementReview action items). Without the `init.assignedTo &&` short-circuit, an item with assignedTo=null/undefined throws a TypeError inside Array.prototype.flatMap, which is NOT caught by the outer internal try/catch (that only wraps the Promise.all, not the post-processing flatMap below it) and would crash the whole /api/tasks request for every user in the org.
preconditions: A ManagementReview document exists with one actionItem whose assignedTo is null (e.g. never assigned) mixed in with items that ARE assigned to the requesting user
A ContinuousImprovement document exists with an analogous unassigned initiative
steps: Call getMyTasks for the user who owns the other, properly-assigned action items/initiatives in the same parent documents
Confirm the request completes successfully
expectedResult: No TypeError is thrown; the null-assignedTo action item and initiative are silently skipped (they don't match `item.assignedTo && ...`), while the properly-assigned items still appear correctly in the response.

title: normalisePriority defaults unknown, missing, and mis-cased values to 'medium'
description: normalisePriority lower-cases the input and checks membership in {'low','medium','high','critical'}; anything else (including a value that only differs by casing, e.g. 'High') falls through to the 'medium' default since the raw value 'High' with its original casing is never in the VALID set — only the lower-cased form is checked for membership, and the ORIGINAL (not lower-cased) value is never returned, so case normalisation itself is not lossy, but any caller expecting 'High' to pass through untouched would be wrong.
steps: Call normalisePriority('critical')
Call normalisePriority('High')
Call normalisePriority(undefined)
Call normalisePriority('urgent')
expectedResult: 'critical' -> 'critical'. 'High' -> 'high' (lower-cased then matched). undefined -> 'medium'. 'urgent' (not in the valid set even lower-cased) -> 'medium'.
